name: Filler Word Sterility
description: Analyzes the frequency and contextual necessity of filler words (e.g., 'essentially', 'basically', 'actually', 'just'). AI models naturally generate highly direct, clinically efficient text completely stripped of conversational padding.
algorithm: Lexical Padding Density & Conversational Fluency Analysis
mechanism: Human speech and writing are naturally imperfect. We use filler words (lexical padding) to pause, gather thoughts, or soften the delivery of information ('It's just that basically…', 'We actually found that…'). Large Language Models, however, do not think in real-time the way humans do; they calculate the next most statistically probable token. Because they are optimized for maximal utility and conciseness via RLHF training, their default output is 'sterilized'. They do not need to pause to 'gather their thoughts', nor do they naturally inject conversational softeners unless explicitly simulating a specific persona. This algorithm calculates the 'Padding Density' of the text by measuring the ratio of unnecessary filler and transition words against the core semantic content. If a text reads with the clinical, hyper-efficient directness of a machine—completely devoid of the linguistic 'crumbs' humans drop while thinking—it is flagged for algorithmic sterility.
useCase: Essential for evaluating casual writing, personal essays, blog posts, and emails where human writers naturally rely on filler words for pacing and tone.
strengths:
• Highly effective at catching AI trying to write personal narratives or casual emails, as the model's inherent drive for efficiency overrides the prompt's request for casualness.
• Captures a fundamental difference in how humans and machines generate language: humans construct language temporally (with pauses), machines construct language probabilistically.
• Resilient against basic synonym-swapping, as it measures the presence of an entire class of functionally useless (but conversationally vital) words.
limitations:
• Susceptible to false positives on professionally edited human text (like journalism or corporate press releases) where editors specifically hunt down and delete filler words.
• Can be bypassed by a user explicitly prompting the AI with 'use a lot of filler words like basically and just'.
• Not effective on short, highly technical text where filler words are naturally absent.
parameters:
Analysis: Lexical Padding Density & Conversational Softener Extraction
Metric: Ratio of Non-Semantic Filler Words to Core Subject Matter
Output: 0-100 Lexical Sterility (Algorithmic Efficiency) Score
accuracy: Moderate to High — 75-85% on casual and persuasive texts. It acts as an excellent behavioral polygraph for 'clinical efficiency' mandated by AI alignment training.

references.title: Uchendu, A. et al. (2020). Authorship Attribution for Neural Text Generation. EMNLP.
Guo, B. et al. (2023). How Close is ChatGPT to Human Experts? Comparison Corpus, Evaluation, and Detection. NeurIPS.
